newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's exports expected to stage comeback in 1996 H2.
newsitem.headline: HK's exports expected to stage comeback in 1996 H2.

text.p: Hong Kong's exports are expected to recover in the second half of 1996 with a rebound in the global economy, according to the latest issue of the Hang Seng Economic Monthly.
Total exports would grow by six percent for the year of 1996, despite sluggish growth of 4.9 percent in the first seven months, it said.
However, the growth would be much slower than the 14.9 percent registered in last year, it added.

The monthly attributed the rosy outlook on improvement in Sino-Taiwan relations, speeding up of tax rebate reimbursements to China's exporters, the partial relaxation of credit conditions in China in recent months, interest rate cuts by the Bundesbank and other European central banks and by falling unemployment and rising income growth in the U.S.
